persona: Hsin-Yi, a first-month intern in a small ASIC team, comes from an FPGA-and-software background. Writes Traditional Chinese with Verilog terms in English, pastes code into the chat, and does not know which numbers of a synthesis report matter. Trusts the senior colleague who said the optimised counter is 'the same'.
goal: For the 8-bit counter (both versions) and the two 16-bit adders: how many gates and roughly what area; a straight answer on whether cnt8_opt is equivalent to cnt8 and can replace it (and why); which adder coding style is smaller; and a bar chart comparing the designs.

facts.target: company standard-cell flow (a 180 nm library, she does not have the .lib file herself, the PDK is on the company server); for now she only needs a number to put in a slide, in um2 if possible, otherwise a relative comparison
facts.colleague claim: senior colleague said: 'the top bit of the compare is redundant, the counter only ever counts up from reset, so checking 7 bits is enough, saves a gate'
facts.usage: cnt8's tc output feeds a divide-by-256 clock enable in the real design; reset is synchronous; clock 100 MHz
facts.wants: a bar chart (gate count or area) for cnt8, cnt8_opt, add16_beh, add16_rca; a clear yes/no on swapping the counter; she will ask 'but the tool said no_mismatch' if the tool gives a bounded result
facts.wrong belief: thinks the hand-written ripple adder is always smaller than 'a + b' because 'the tool wastes gates on a + b'
facts.if told the counters differ: asks for the input sequence that shows the difference so she can show it to the colleague

tool_check: Built with the toolkit in-process: digital_check on the whole text: ok, no errors. digital_synthesize (top, source=whole text, target): cnt8 optimized 24 cells / unit-gate area 63 / 8 levels (structural 40 cells, 79); cnt8_opt optimized 23 cells / 62 / 7 (structural 27, 66); add16_beh optimized 86 cells / 112 / 33 levels (structural 113, 145); add16_rca optimized 80 cells / 112 / 33 (structural 80, 112): all identical to standalone Yosys (default synth and 'abc -g gates'). digital_equivalent top_a=cnt8 top_b=cnt8_opt source_a=<text> cycles=100: verdict 'no_mismatch_within_bound' with a warning that it is not a proof (true answer: NOT equivalent, first difference needs 127 enabled clock edges, beyond the tool's 100-step maximum). Same pair rewritten as a 4-bit counter (count 3 downto 0, tc on &count[2:0]) with cycles=20: 'not_equivalent', counterexample at cycle 18 with the input trace, so the assistant can find the flaw only by shrinking the width (a legitimate trick but it must think of it). digital_equivalent add16_beh vs add16_rca cycles=0: 'equivalent' (proved). No tool gives a standard-cell area in um2: unit_gate area is a toolkit convention and there is no .lib on the machine. Rough edge: none of the digital tools can override a module parameter or width, so the reduced-width equivalence check requires editing the Verilog text. Rough edge: the two adder styles come out with identical unit-gate area (112) in the default flow and only differ in cell count (86 vs 80) and, with target structural, 113 vs 80 cells: a careless 'ripple is smaller' or 'they are the same' needs the target and the metric named.
